cls: Prostaglandin E2 - oxytocic / cervical ripening agent
quick: Endocervical gel: 0.5 mg PGE2 intracervically; may repeat after 6 h, max 1.5 mg (3 doses) in 24 h
Used in pregnancy for its obstetric indication (cervical ripening at/near term) under hospital supervision
Not relevant to peripartum use; minimal data
No specific adjustment for this short obstetric use
No specific adjustment for this short obstetric use
Continuous uterine activity and fetal heart rate monitoring; watch for hyperstimulation
summary: Dinoprostone is prostaglandin E2 used for ripening an unfavorable cervix in pregnant women at or near term who need labor induction. The endocervical gel (PREPIDIL, 0.5 mg) stimulates the gravid myometrium and softens the cervix. It is FOR HOSPITAL USE ONLY, requiring continuous uterine and fetal heart-rate monitoring because of the risk of uterine hyperstimulation, hypertonus and fetal distress; uterine rupture and (rarely) amniotic fluid embolism have occurred.
indications: Ripening of an unfavorable cervix in pregnant women at or near term with a medical or obstetrical need for labor induction

dosage.n: Use 20 mm catheter if no effacement, 10 mm if 50% effaced

dosage.d: May repeat 0.5 mg if response inadequate, at intervals of 6 hours
dosage.n: Maximum 1.5 mg (3 doses) in a 24-hour period

dosage.d: Delay oxytocin per labeling after the last gel dose
dosage.n: Wait recommended interval (e.g., 6-12 h) before oxytocin

admin: FOR HOSPITAL USE ONLY by clinicians with immediate access to intensive care and acute surgical facilities
Bring the gel to room temperature naturally before use - do not force-warm with a water bath or microwave
Administer endocervically with the patient supine; have her remain recumbent for 15-30 minutes
Use caution to prevent skin contact and wash hands thoroughly after administration
Provide continuous uterine activity and fetal heart-rate monitoring during use
moa: Dinoprostone is prostaglandin E2. Administered endocervically it stimulates the myometrium of the gravid uterus to contract similarly to term labor and promotes cervical ripening by altering the cervical extracellular matrix (collagen degradation and increased hydration), softening, effacing and dilating the cervix. It also stimulates gastrointestinal smooth muscle (causing occasional vomiting/diarrhea) and can lower blood pressure and raise body temperature at higher doses.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to prostaglandins or gel constituents

Situations where prolonged uterine contraction is inappropriate: prior cesarean section or major uterine surgery, cephalopelvic disproportion, history of difficult/traumatic delivery, grand multiparity (>=6 term pregnancies), non-vertex presentation, hyperactive/hypertonic uterus, fetal distress where delivery is not imminent
Placenta previa or unexplained vaginal bleeding this pregnancy
Vaginal delivery not indicated (e.g., vasa previa, active genital herpes)
relative: Asthma, glaucoma, or raised intraocular pressure
Women >=30 yr, complications in pregnancy, or gestation >40 weeks (increased postpartum DIC risk)
monitor: Signs of hypersensitivity or amniotic fluid embolism

preg: Dinoprostone is used during pregnancy for its labeled obstetric indication (cervical ripening at or near term when labor induction is indicated). It is not for use earlier in pregnancy for this product and must be given under hospital supervision.
lact: Lactation considerations are not applicable to this short peripartum use; data on breast milk are limited and a single peripartum dose is not expected to be clinically significant.
renal: No specific dose adjustment for this short-term obstetric use, though caution is advised in significant renal disease.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment for this short-term obstetric use, though caution is advised in significant hepatic disease.

major: Oxytocin and other oxytocics (additive/potentiated uterotonic effect - do not use concurrently; observe recommended interval before starting oxytocin)
minor: NSAIDs (prostaglandin synthesis inhibitors may theoretically blunt effect)
interactions.diagnostics: May transiently elevate body temperature and white cell count; can lower blood pressure at higher exposure

serious: Uterine hyperstimulation / hypertonus with fetal distress
rare: Amniotic fluid embolism (Anaphylactoid Syndrome of Pregnancy)
emergency: Severe uterine hyperstimulation with fetal compromise

monitoring: Continuous uterine activity (tone and contraction frequency)
Postpartum coagulation/fibrinolysis in at-risk women (age >=30, complications, >40 weeks)
counsel: This medicine softens the cervix to help start labor and is given in hospital where you and the baby are closely monitored
You may feel warmth in the vagina, mild cramping, back pain, or have some nausea
Tell your care team at once about strong or constant contractions, severe pain, or bleeding
Continuous monitoring of your contractions and the baby's heartbeat is needed during treatment
pk: Cervical softening over hours; uterine activity may begin within ~30-60 minutes of the gel
Local effect builds over several hours after endocervical placement
Dinoprostone is rapidly metabolized (plasma half-life of minutes); effect outlasts plasma levels
Cervical effect persists several hours; assess before repeat dosing at 6 hours
Store under continuous refrigeration at 2-8 C (36-46 F)
pearls: FOR HOSPITAL USE ONLY - requires continuous uterine and fetal heart-rate monitoring because of the risk of uterine hyperstimulation, hypertonus and fetal distress
Do not give concurrently with oxytocin; observe the labeled interval before starting oxytocin to avoid additive uterotonic effects
Uterine rupture and rare amniotic fluid embolism (Anaphylactoid Syndrome of Pregnancy) can occur; women >=30 yr, with complications, or >40 weeks have higher postpartum DIC risk
Bring gel to room temperature naturally; refrigerate the product and do not force-warm it
missed: Not applicable - dinoprostone is administered by clinicians on a defined schedule during cervical ripening/labor induction in hospital, not self-dosed.
overdose: Overdose or excessive effect manifests as uterine hyperstimulation/hypertonus with potential fetal distress and, in severe cases, uterine rupture. Management: stop the prostaglandin, remove any retained gel/insert if possible, position the mother on her side, give oxygen and IV fluids, and administer a tocolytic (e.g., a beta-agonist) for hyperstimulation; proceed to expedited/operative delivery if fetal compromise persists.
